enso.cpc_discussion: ENSO Alert System Status: El Niño Advisory   Synopsis:   El Niño continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than an 83% chance). El Niño strengthened further last month, with sea surface temperature anomalies exceeding +4.0°C in portions of the eastern equatorial Pacific [Fig. 1] . Most Niño indices increased in the past month, reaching +2.1°C in Niño-3.4, +3.0°C in Niño-3, and +3.9°C in Niño-1+2 [Fig. 2] . The equatorial subsurface temperature index (average from 180°-100°W) was well above average [Fig. 3] , reflecting a deeper-than-average thermocline. Subsurface temperatures remained in excess of +10.0°C at depth in the eastern Pacific Ocean [Fig. 4] . Low-level westerly wind anomalies and upper-level easterly wind anomalies stretched from the western to the east-central equatorial Pacific. Enhanced convection and rainfall persisted from the central to the eastern Pacific, while anomalies remained suppressed over Indonesia [Fig. 5] . The traditional and equatorial Southern Oscillation indices were significantly negative. Collectively, the coupled ocean-atmosphere system reflected a strengthening El Niño. The CPC Official ENSO outlook , which synthesizes multiple models from North America and abroad, indicates El Niño will continue to strengthen through the end of the year [Figs. 6 -7 -8] . notes: Wind/gust ranges: quantile-boosted models widened by a conformal margin fit on out-of-fold errors (days 1-10 ensemble model).

Temperature ranges: NBM high/low plus the empirical error distribution (by lead day and season) measured at Alamogordo, Holloman and Las Cruces airports; the same error spread is assumed at Hawk St, the Pass and Cloudcroft (mountain sites are not verified).
Rain: percentile amounts come from the hurdle model; coverage above nominal mostly reflects the large share of dry days. Cloudcroft days 8-10 slightly under-cover (88% vs 90%).
Test period: Jul 2025 – Oct 2026 (about 15 months), so coverage numbers carry a few points of sampling noise.

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service El Paso TX/Santa Teresa NM
516 AM MDT Mon Oct 26 2026

...New AVIATION, FIRE WEATHER...

.KEY MESSAGES... 
Updated at 530 AM MDT Mon Oct 26 2026

 - Isolated showers and thunderstorms continue east of El Paso
   this evening, mostly over Hudspeth and Otero Counties. A few
   storms may be strong and capable of localized flooding. 
 
 - A brief stretch of drier weather through Wednesday before rain
   chances return Thursday into next weekend.

 - Typical late-October temperatures, with lowland highs in the
   lower to mid 70s.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 1100 PM MDT Sun Oct 25 2026

Another night, another round of severe thunderstorms and heavy 
rain. The good news is that the upper level trough and surface 
convergence that has lead to multiple nights of severe weather are
finally moving to the east, but not before we could see one more 
round of strong thunderstorms on Monday. The main threat for these
strong thunderstorms will be in Hudspeth County. Most of the 
region will stay rain free on Monday. High temperatures on Monday 
will run a few degrees below average.

For Tuesday and Wednesday we will see drier air move into the 
area on a zonal (west to east) flow aloft. We look to stay dry 
both days with high temperatures climbing a few degrees above 
average by Wednesday. Wednesday afternoon our upper level flow 
will begin to turn more to the southeast as our next upper level 
trough approaches the west coast. Our precipitable water values 
(PW's) will drop below 0.5 for most of the area on Tuesday and 
Wednesday. But then on Thursday, we will see another surge of 
moisture from the south and southeast and we will see PW's jump to
around 0.80 to 0.90 by Thursday. With the moisture in place and 
the next upper level trough approaching the area will be enough to
give us a chance for thunderstorms Thursday afternoon and 
evening. On Friday the main energy from the upper level trough 
will sweep across New Mexico and that will give us a good chance 
for thunderstorms. With the well above average PW's we could see 
some heavy rain makers which can lead to isolated flash flooding. 
High temperatures for both Thursday and Friday will run near 
seasonal averages. Right now next Saturday and Sunday look dry, 
with high temperatures near average. 

&&

.AVIATION...
(12Z TAFS)
Issued at 530 AM MDT Mon Oct 26 2026

VMC today with light surface winds AOB 5 knots. Skies FEW- 
SCT070, SCT-BKN250. Isolated TS across SE NM and W TX this 
evening, between 00-06Z. No direct impacts expected for KELP or 
NM sites.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 530 AM MDT Mon Oct 26 2026

Dry conditions for Gila NF, but isolated thunderstorms are 
expected across Lincoln NF this evening. Light south winds today,
generally less than 5 mph. A few hours of Fair vent rates this 
afternoon, but most of the day will be Poor. A brief window of dry
conditions area wide exists Tuesday and Wednesday. Rain chances 
return Thursday through next weekend, leading to another round of 
wetting precipitation over the forested areas. ERCs are very low 
at the moment, so no fire danger expected into early November.

&&
